[Bugfix][Qwen4Exp] Reserve QSA indexer prefill workspace during memory profiling

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Reserve the Qwen4Exp QSA indexer's selection scratch (prefill logits workspace, or the worst-case decode logits,
whichever is larger) during the memory-profiling run, so the KV pool is not sized past what the indexer needs at
runtime. Fixes #60489.

## Claims

- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`Qwen4Exp`) no longer OOMs inside `qsa_select_paged_prefill` on the first long prefill
  when `--max-model-len` and `--gpu-memory-utilization` are high: the profiler now accounts for the indexer
  logits workspace (`VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB`, 512 MiB by default) plus the 1 MiB top-k workspace.
- Configurations that genuinely do not fit are rejected at startup with the existing actionable
  "estimated maximum model length" error instead of failing at request time.
- The decode path is covered too: `qsa_select_paged_decode` allocates `[decode tokens, compressed columns]` fp32
  logits on demand, which exceeds the 512 MiB prefill budget above 2048 decode tokens per step at 262K (e.g.
  `max_num_seqs` 1024 with MTP K=3). The reservation is `max(prefill budget, worst-case decode logits)` plus the
  top-k workspace, like `sparse_attn_indexer`.
- ~25 lines in the QSA profiling branch (`vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/qsa.py`); no core/runner changes.

## Validation

`Intel/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AutoRound`, 4× RTX 3090 (SM86), TP=4 + EP, nightly `0.30.1rc1.dev702`
(this file set is unchanged on current `main`):

```bash
vllm serve Intel/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AutoRound --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 262144 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.96 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 --max-num-seqs 32 --cpu-offload-gb 2 --cpu-offload-params visual
# then one ~250K-token chat request
```

| default 512 MiB indexer budget | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Available KV memory / GPU | 3.32 GiB | 2.93 GiB (workspace accounted) |
| Startup | succeeds | fails fast: "estimated maximum model length is 236400. Try increasing `gpu_memory_utilization` …" |
| First long prefill | OOM in `qsa_select_paged_prefill` (512 MiB requested, 168 MiB free)¹ | n/a (rejected up front) |

¹ Reproduced with `--language-model-only` in place of the two offload flags (3.49 GiB KV/GPU), same OOM site.

With `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB=128` the fixed build starts at 262K and the profiler's numbers hold at
runtime: a c=1/8/32 decode sweep and a 300-question GSM8K/MMLU-Pro eval run with no OOM; in a build that also
carried #60491 (fp8_e5m2 KV) and the #53981 rebase, two 250K-token passkey requests (depth 0.5 and 0.1) pass. Output is unaffected (the change only runs in the profiling branch).

Decode worst case (eager decode, no CUDA graphs, `--language-model-only`, `--max-num-seqs 128`,
`VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB=16` so decode dominates), instrumented with a test-only log line:

| | first commit (prefill only) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Reserved during profiling | 16 MiB + 1 MiB | **33,587,200 B** + 1 MiB (formula) |
| Real decode logits at runtime (128 concurrent requests) | up to 31,225,600 B (119 rows × 65,600 cols), **not reserved** | ≤ 33,587,200 B (128 × 65,600), covered |
| KV pool / c=128 load / 250K passkey | 283,825 tokens / pass | 283,825 tokens / pass (×2 runs) / pass |

The formula's worst-case width (`cdiv(max_model_len, block_size) × cdiv(block_size, compress_ratio)` = 65,600 at
262K, block size 1600) matched the runtime decode logits exactly. The old version did not OOM here (the 16 MB
shortfall fit in allocator slack); at larger `max_num_seqs` × speculative tokens the shortfall grows into
hundreds of MB. The final inlined code was re-run in the same config: identical KV pool, c=128 ×2, c=1/8/32 sweep
and a 250K passkey all pass with no OOM.

`pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD`: all hooks pass.

No unit test added: the behaviour is the profiler's view of peak GPU memory during the dummy run, which a CPU
unit test cannot observe; CI has no Qwen3.8-Flash-Next long-context job. Validation above was done outside CI.

## Details

Root cause: the profiling dummy run carries no attention metadata, so `Qwen4ExpQSA.forward` takes the
`not isinstance(metadata, dict)` branch and returns before the indexer runs. `qsa_select_paged_prefill`
allocates its logits workspace on demand ("always allocate the worst case"), so the profiler never sees it.
The generic `sparse_attn_indexer` already handles the same situation with a dummy allocation of
`max(decode logits, prefill cap)` in its own no-metadata branch; this mirrors that inline in the QSA profiling
branch (review feedback: inlined rather than a single-use helper). QSA attention runs eagerly outside CUDA-graph
capture (`@eager_break_during_capture`), so the reservation never lands in a graph pool.

Tradeoff, by design: the KV pool shrinks by the memory the indexer really needs (~0.4 GiB/GPU here at the
default budget). Users can trade that back by lowering `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB`; the indexer chunks
rows to fit. The reservation is freed immediately and only runs during profiling, so there is no steady-state
cost and no added host/device synchronization.

Duplicate check: searched open issues/PRs for the QSA indexer/profiling area (`qsa indexer`,
`VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB`, `qsa_select_paged_prefill`); no existing report or fix.

(Claude Code). I reviewed the diff and ran the validation above on my own hardware.

[Bugfix] Fuse GLM-5.3 KDA q|k|v convs into one conv1d parameter

## Overview

`Glm5NextLinearAttention` cached the merged q|k|v conv weight on the first forward, so an RL refit left the conv kernels reading stale values (#55087). This PR replaces the three `q/k/v_conv1d` modules with a single `conv1d` parameter of shape `[3 * C_local, 1, K]`, which the kernels read directly. Checkpoint `q_conv1d` / `k_conv1d` / `v_conv1d` weights load into it as shards 0/1/2 through `stacked_params_mapping`, using the `_make_fused_conv1d_weight_loader` already used by Kimi-Linear KDA and OLMo-Hybrid GDN. There is no second tensor to keep in sync, so every write path lands in the tensor the kernels read, at a fixed address.

Alternative fixes for the same issue: #56298 and #57638 (see Details; their authors are co-authors on the commit). The fused-parameter design was suggested by hao-aaron in review and replaces this PR's first approach (parameter views into a merged buffer), which broke under weight offloading and `ipc_cache` copy mode.

## Claims

- After `load_weights` / `reload_weights` (checkpoint or kernel format), GLM-5.3 KDA decode uses the refitted conv weights, in eager mode **and** with the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` cudagraphs.
- The conv weight keeps its address across refits, so FULL decode graphs captured before a refit stay valid.
- Works with `--cpu-offload-gb` (with and without refit) and with `--load-format ipc_cache` in both `copy` and `zero_copy` modes.
- No numerical change: the per-rank layout is `[q_r | k_r | v_r]`, the same as the old `torch.cat`. Direct-load outputs are identical to `main`. One copy of the conv weights is dropped.

## Validation

Hardware: GB300 (SM100), TP1, 4-layer pruned GLM-5.3-Flash at full width (`JaredforReal/GLM-5.3-Flash-4L`).

```
pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_conv_weight_refit.py tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py -v
```

- Unit tests (CPU, `conv1d` sub-module): checkpoint q/k/v shards (2D and 3D) land in q|k|v order; `load_weights`-style refit and a real `initialize_layerwise_reload` / `finalize_layerwise_reload` cycle update the weight without moving it. 22 passed with `test_kda_recurrent.py`.
- `test_refit_reaches_cudagraph_decode[cpu_offload_gb=0|10]` (pruned model, default cudagraphs, one engine per case): direct load -> reference tokens; `reload_weights` of the checkpoint with the conv weights x2 -> output changes; checkpoint as-is -> == reference; kernel-format `reload_weights(is_checkpoint_format=False)` on `conv1d.weight` x2 / x0.5 -> changes / == reference; the conv weight address is identical after all four refits. 2 passed (~5 min each, mostly startup). On `main` the first refit step fails (#55087).
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: passed (ruff, mypy, SPDX, test tethering).

CI note: the e2e test is the first in `tests/models/glm5next` to use the pruned checkpoint (19 GB download, needs SM90/SM100, skipped elsewhere). It runs in the existing `glm5next-unit-tests` step; the two offload cases take about 10 min together on GB300, mostly engine startup. #57537 adds a dedicated step for pruned-checkpoint e2e tests that this test could move to once it lands.

Full refit flow, 3 prompts x 24 greedy tokens, compared with `main` direct load:

| tree | config | direct load | dummy -> `reload_weights()` | `load_weights` partial update / kernel-format refit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | cudagraphs | reference | wrong (#55087) | wrong |
| previous revision (buffer views) | cudagraphs | == main | == main | == main |
| previous revision (buffer views) | `cpu_offload_gb=10` | **wrong** | – | – |
| this PR | cudagraphs | == main | == main | == main |
| this PR | eager | == main | == main | == main |
| this PR | `cpu_offload_gb=10` | == main | – | – |

After the reload, every language-model parameter and buffer checksum equals a fresh load.

`--load-format ipc_cache` (a `vllm preload` daemon per GPU, default cudagraphs). After each refit the check compares the conv weight the kernel reads against the checkpoint × scale (max abs diff), then compares the output:

| tree | mode | load | kernel-format refit x2 / x1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | copy | == main | weight stale (diff 0.72), output unchanged (#55087) |
| previous revision (buffer views) | copy | == main | **weight stale (diff 0.72), output unchanged** |
| previous revision (buffer views) | zero_copy | == main | diff 0, output changes / == main |
| this PR | copy | == main | diff 0, output changes / == main, address unchanged |
| this PR | zero_copy | == main | diff 0, output changes / == main, address unchanged |

Checkpoint-format refits are not supported on an `ipc_cache`-loaded model on `main` either, so they're not compared here. `_apply_entries` re-registers every parameter as a plain `nn.Parameter` (399/399 lose `weight_loader`), so `load_weights` of any stacked weight raises `AttributeError` (verified on `main` with `self_attn.q_proj`), and the layerwise `reload_weights` fails with `Cannot copy out of meta tensor`. On `main` the three conv weights happened to fall through to `default_weight_loader`; with this PR they're stacked like the other projections. Making checkpoint-format refit work after `ipc_cache` is a separate issue.

## Details

**Root cause.** The KDA layer runs one causal conv over the concatenated q|k|v channels. The merged weight was built lazily on the first forward with `torch.cat` and cached, so later writes to `q/k/v_conv1d.weight` (RL refit through the weight-transfer engines, `reload_weights`, or kernel-format `copy_`) never reached it.

**Why not invalidate the cache (#56298, #57638).** Both PRs drop the cached tensor on refit and rebuild it on the next forward. That works with `enforce_eager=True`, but with the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` cudagraphs the KDA forward is captured inside the FULL decode graphs, which keep the old tensor's address, so decode replays never see the rebuilt weight.

**Why one parameter instead of views into a merged buffer.** Views only hold while nothing replaces a parameter's storage. The UVA and prefetch CPU offloaders set each parameter's `.data` right after the layer is built, and the `ipc_cache` loader in copy mode clones every entry separately; either way the three weights stop aliasing the tensor the kernels read. With a single parameter, those paths, the layerwise reload, and kernel-format `copy_` all write the tensor the kernels use. This matches how Kimi-Linear and OLMo-Hybrid already store their fused short convs.

**Trade-offs.**
- The vLLM parameter name changes from `q/k/v_conv1d.weight` to `conv1d.weight`. Checkpoint-format updates keep the HF names and go through the stacked mapping. Kernel-format writers need the fused name, and GLM-5.3 artifacts saved with vLLM parameter names (`sharded_state`, vLLM-serialized tensorizer) before this change will not load.
- Open PRs #59304 (KCP) and #57496 (CPU KDA backend) reference `q_conv1d` / `_merged_conv_weight` and will need a small rebase.

**Not covered here.** The TP2 cudagraph reload drift from the FlashInfer TRT-LLM FP8 MoE `gemm1_clamp_limit` tensor and the DSA indexer's lazily cached `_wp_fp32` are separate issues, left for follow-ups.

@@ -0,0 +1,133 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""GLM-5.3-Flash KDA q|k|v short convs are one fused parameter.
+
+The conv kernels read ``conv1d.weight`` directly, so an RL refit must reach it
+through every write path (#55087), and FULL cudagraphs capture its address, so
+it must never move.
+"""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.layerwise import (
+    finalize_layerwise_reload,
+    initialize_layerwise_reload,
+    record_metadata_for_reloading,
+)
+from vllm.models.glm5next.common import kda
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.gdn_attn import GDNAttentionMetadata
+
+CHANNELS, KERNEL = 8, 4
+
+
+def _checkpoint_weights(seed: int) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
+    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    return [torch.randn(CHANNELS, 1, KERNEL, generator=gen) for _ in range(3)]
+
+
+def _load(conv1d: nn.Module, weights: list[torch.Tensor]) -> None:
+    for shard_id, weight in enumerate(weights):
+        conv1d.weight.weight_loader(conv1d.weight, weight, shard_id)
+
+
+def _kernel_view(conv1d: nn.Module) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return conv1d.weight.view(conv1d.weight.size(0), conv1d.weight.size(-1))
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def conv1d(dist_init) -> nn.Module:
+    return kda._fused_qkv_conv1d(KERNEL, CHANNELS, 1, 0, prefix="conv1d")
+
+
+def test_fused_conv_loads_checkpoint_shards_in_qkv_order(conv1d):
+    weights = _checkpoint_weights(seed=0)
+    _load(conv1d, [w.view(CHANNELS, KERNEL) for w in weights[:1]] + weights[1:])
+    assert conv1d.weight.shape == (3 * CHANNELS, 1, KERNEL)
+    assert torch.equal(_kernel_view(conv1d), torch.cat(weights).squeeze(1))
+
+
+def test_refit_updates_fused_conv_without_moving_it(conv1d):
+    """Refits through load_weights (RL weight sync) and through the layerwise
+    reload (``reload_weights``) both land at the original address."""
+    data_ptr = conv1d.weight.data_ptr()
+    _load(conv1d, _checkpoint_weights(seed=0))
+
+    refit = _checkpoint_weights(seed=1)
+    _load(conv1d, refit)
+    assert torch.equal(_kernel_view(conv1d), torch.cat(refit).squeeze(1))
+
+    reload = _checkpoint_weights(seed=2)
+    model = nn.Sequential(conv1d)
+    record_metadata_for_reloading(model)
+    initialize_layerwise_reload(model)
+    _load(conv1d, reload)
+    finalize_layerwise_reload(model, model_config=None)
+    assert torch.equal(_kernel_view(conv1d), torch.cat(reload).squeeze(1))
+    assert conv1d.weight.data_ptr() == data_ptr
+
+
+def _decode_layer(conv1d: nn.Module) -> kda.Glm5NextLinearAttention:
+    layer = object.__new__(kda.Glm5NextLinearAttention)
+    nn.Module.__init__(layer)
+    layer.prefix = "layer.0"
+    layer.conv1d = conv1d
+    layer.local_num_heads, layer.head_dim = 1, CHANNELS
+    layer.local_projection_size = CHANNELS
+    layer.kda_safe_gate, layer.kda_lower_bound = True, -5.0
+    layer.A_log = layer.dt_bias = None
+    layer._conv_state_dim_first = True
+    layer.kv_cache = (torch.zeros(1, 3 * CHANNELS, KERNEL - 1), None)
+    return layer
+
+
+def test_decode_reads_refitted_fused_conv(conv1d, monkeypatch):
+    """Decode must hand the conv kernel ``conv1d.weight`` itself, not a copy
+    cached by an earlier forward, so refits reach the address FULL cudagraphs
+    capture (#55087)."""
+    layer = _decode_layer(conv1d)
+    metadata = GDNAttentionMetadata(
+        num_prefills=0,
+        num_prefill_tokens=0,
+        num_decodes=1,
+        num_decode_tokens=1,
+        num_spec_decodes=0,
+        num_spec_decode_tokens=0,
+        num_actual_tokens=1,
+        non_spec_query_start_loc=torch.tensor([0, 1], dtype=torch.int32),
+        non_spec_state_indices_tensor=torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32),
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        kda,
+        "get_forward_context",
+        lambda: SimpleNamespace(attn_metadata={layer.prefix: metadata}),
+    )
+    seen = []
+
+    def conv_update(x, conv_state, weight, *args, **kwargs):
+        seen.append(weight)
+        return x
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(kda, "causal_conv1d_update", conv_update)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        kda, "fused_recurrent_kda", lambda **kwargs: (kwargs["out"], None)
+    )
+
+    def decode() -> torch.Tensor:
+        layer._forward(
+            torch.zeros(1, 3 * CHANNELS),
+            torch.zeros(1, 1, 1, CHANNELS),
+            torch.zeros(1, 1, 1),
+            torch.zeros(1, 1, 1, CHANNELS),
+        )
+        return seen.pop()
+
+    for seed in (0, 1):
+        weights = _checkpoint_weights(seed)
+        _load(conv1d, weights)
+        weight = decode()
+        assert weight.data_ptr() == conv1d.weight.data_ptr()
+        assert torch.equal(weight, torch.cat(weights).squeeze(1))

Serialize changelog-file runs per PR branch

While testing #439 in the release-notes playground, opening a PR with a type label started two "Changelog file" runs on the same branch, one for `opened` and one for `labeled`. Both tried to commit. One push failed with `cannot lock ref` and posted the commit-failed comment, and the other run's "entry committed" comment replaced it a few seconds later. Which comment wins depends on timing.

The runs never waited for each other because the concurrency group ended with `workflow_run.id`, so each run had its own group. #41 added that suffix together with `head_repository.full_name` to stop a fork branch from cancelling an internal branch with the same name. The repository name already does that.

This drops the run ID from the group in `release-notes-changelog-file.yml` and `changelog-submit.yml`, and sets `cancel-in-progress: false`. Cancelling is the wrong choice here: a run cancelled after its push but before its comment job would leave the next run with nothing to commit and nothing to post. With queueing, the second run starts after the first, finds nothing new to commit, and records no decision, so it posts nothing.

Tested in docs-playground-release-notes-changelogs with the caller pointed at this branch (now back on `@v1`). On a labeled PR, the second run started at 09:25:58, one second after the first ended, logged "No changes to commit", and skipped the comment job. The PR got one changelog commit and one "entry committed" comment.

Related to elastic/docs-eng-team#1133
